By Gavin van Marle
19 November 2026
M&A returned to the contract logistics sector over the past 24 hours as US-based Neovia Logistics was snapped up by Logisteed and Turkey’s Ekol Logistics was sold to Arvato.
Japanese freight forwarder and 3PL Logisteed is to acquire pure-play contract operator Neovia Logistics, creating a platform for Logisteed to expand into the North American market.
Neovia, which began life as the in-house logistics arm of US heavy equipment manufacturer Caterpillar, has been owned by a group of private equity funds – Oaktree Capital Management, Ares Management, and Vector Capital – since 2022, and has been through series of ownership changes since it was carved-out of its parent company in 2012.
Financial details of the transaction have not been disclosed. However, Neovia’s 2025 adjusted revenues were recorded at $589m, with EBITDA of $66m, and has a current roster of just under 6,000 employees.
According to Logisteed, there will be little overlap between the activities of the two companies, with 54% of Neovia’s revenue coming from North America, 40% from Europe and just 6% from Asia-Pacific. In contrast, Logisteed earns 71% of its turnover from Asia-Pacific, 19% from Europe, and 10% from North America.
However, Logisteed, in which Japan Post acquired a 20% stake last year, is a far bigger enterprise, recording revenue of around $6.2bn in calendar year 2025.
It said new markets and new supply chain capabilities were a key feature of the acquisition.
“Logisteed customers gain deeper North American and European contract logistics capabilities, while Neovia customers gain access to Logisteed’s APAC network and broader transportation and forwarding capabilities,” it said.
It added that shippers would be offered “a more comprehensive suite of integrated supply chain solutions by combining both companies’ expertise in contract logistics with Logisteed’s forwarding, transportation, and other functions.”
Neovia chief executive Mike Fahy said: “Today marks the start of an exciting new chapter for Neovia, our customers, and our people.
“Logisteed shares our commitment to operational excellence and to the people who deliver it every day, and we are excited to continue our journey together – our leadership team will remain in place, and our priorities do not change,” he added.
The deal is expected to close at the end of the first quarter next year.
Elsewhere, German supply chain management and e-commerce logistic provider Arvato announced today it had agreed to acquire Turkey’s Ekol Logistics – the remaining domestic operation, not sold to Danish ferry operator DFDS is early 2025.
Arvato, part of Germany’s Bertlesmann Gourp, said the deal would expand its Turkish footprint to 1.2m sq metres of logistics space across 26 warehouses, and “further strengthen Arvato’s position in fashion and consumer electronics logistics” plus “establishes a significant presence in healthcare logistics and provides an attractive entry point into the FMCG sector”.
Frank Schirrmeister, Arvato CEO, added: “By combining Arvato’s international network with Ekol’s strong local platform, we are creating new opportunities for growth, greater operational flexibility, and enhanced supply chain performance for our clients.
“At the same time, the transaction underscores our ambition to invest in markets where we see long-term growth opportunities and where we can create tangible value for our clients,” he added.
The deal value was undisclosed, and completion remains subject to regulatory approval.
